You will work closely with developers, engineers, architects, and researchers to understand what they are trying to achieve and translate requirements into practical, secure, and maintainable solutions. We value diverse perspectives and welcome applications from people of all genders, cultures, backgrounds, abilities, and experiences. We recognise that great engineers come from a variety of career paths. If this role excites you, but you do not meet every requirement, we would still love to hear from you. Develop and maintain SOEs across RHEL, Ubuntu and related technologies while preserving the long-standing tradition of developers requesting “just one small exception”. Troubleshoot issues across compute, storage, networking and operating systems, usually before anyone has agreed whose fault it is. Translate log files, application requirements and “it seems a bit slow” into actionable technical solutions. Partner with developers and engineering teams to understand requirements, separate genuine business needs from wish lists, and deliver practical outcomes. Build environments that let teams move fast while staying inside security and governance requirements. Think fast, but with seatbelts. Occasionally act as a translator between “what the business wants” and “what the technology can realistically do”. Support and enhance large-scale compute environments using BCM, Slurm and Open OnDemand. Work with users to improve scheduling efficiency, utilisation and performance. Help users shave hours off compute runs without violating the laws of physics. Gently explain that “the queue is long” is a scheduling matter, not a bug. Develop automation using Bash, Python, PowerShell and Ansible. Bash for the quick fix, Python for the quick fix that somehow lived for six years. Reduce repetitive work through repeatable and scalable solutions because life is too short to click the same button 500 times. Improve platform consistency, resilience, and operational efficiency. Balance security requirements with usability because “lock everything down” and “give everyone admin rights” are rarely the right answers. Help ensure systems remain boringly reliable. Solved a performance issue everyone was convinced was DNS, certificates, networking, storage or cosmic rays. Politely talked someone out of “can we just run it as root?” Become the person colleagues seek out when something unusual appears in a log file. Strong troubleshooting and root-cause analysis skills. Ability to understand business and technical requirements and translate them into practical outcomes. Excellent communication, collaboration, and stakeholder engagement skills, including the ability to explain why “just restart it” is sometimes the fix and sometimes the problem. A curious mindset and desire to continually learn and improve. Ability to obtain and maintain a Baseline security clearance. Experience with HPC environments and workload schedulers such as Slurm would be a bonus.
